content.text:
I submitted index 7 (Bi 0.34, Cu 0.27, V 0.39). It had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured: 17.6 µA. I used all 3 photocurrent measurements, so 114 of the 117 compositions were never measured. I can't say how close index 7 is to the best one in the library.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.41 / 0.19 / 0.40 | 11.8 µA |
| **7** | **0.34 / 0.27 / 0.39** | **17.6 µA** |
| 92 | 0.30 / 0.35 / 0.35 | 0.03 µA |

- **Where I started:** index 2, which has equal Bi and V. That's the region where BiVO₄, a known photoanode material, should form.
- **XRD:** I used 4 of the 5 XRD scans. Indices 2, 7 and 0 all show peaks matching BiVO₄ (at Q ≈ 1.35, 2.03 and 2.15). All four scans are dominated by an unidentified peak at Q ≈ 2.78.
- **Trend:** adding Cu raised photocurrent from index 2 to index 7. I then stepped further toward Cu with index 92, and the photocurrent collapsed almost to zero. So the peak is probably near index 7, and it may be narrow.

Compositions I ruled out without measuring photocurrent:
- **Index 93** (Bi 0.25 / Cu 0.36 / V 0.40): its XRD showed much weaker BiVO₄ peaks.
- **Index 0** (Bi 0.28 / Cu 0.24 / V 0.48): its XRD showed an extra phase at Q ≈ 1.74, possibly a copper vanadate.

Compositions near index 7, such as 74 (Bi 0.36 / Cu 0.26 / V 0.38) or 76 (Bi 0.27 / Cu 0.30 / V 0.43), may do better but were never measured. The Cu-rich and Cu-V corners of the library weren't tested at all.
